brief: Bernstein extends its AI data center pod-cost model from Nvidia Blackwell/Vera Rubin to AMD and ASIC architectures. It cuts Vera Rubin to $7.5M per rack (from $9.1M), driven by lower per-rack NAND assumptions and more conservative HBM4 pricing, now near the $7-8M supply-chain consensus. AMD's MI455X lands at $7.3M, similar overall: AMD earns lower GPU margins (less compute content) but higher CPU value than Nvidia's Vera, and higher networking content from up to 3 NICs per GPU. OpenAI's Jalapeno is put at $5.0M per pod; unlike expected, it is not a white-label Nvidia design but expands the scale-up domain and keeps data in HBM/DRAM rather than scale-out/NAND. Google's TPU v7 Ironwood is estimated at $2.7M but with low conviction given sparse disclosure. Capex/GW ranges $35B (Jalapeno) to ~$40B (Vera Rubin). Implied 2026-27 GW shipments (36GW to 43GW) run well above Bernstein's own US data-center capacity model (18GW to 26GW), which it attributes to growing international buildout (e.g., OpenAI-Firmus in APAC) amid US siting delays.
